references.text: In Psalm 40:6-8, David expresses a willingness to do God's will, which reflects Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane that God's will be done, even in the face of suffering.
In Isaiah 53:10, it is prophesied about the Lord's servant who would suffer, foreshadowing Jesus' suffering and submission to God's will in Mark 14:35.
In Hebrews 5:7, Jesus' prayers and tears during his suffering are reflected, corresponding with his prayer in Gethsemane.
In Luke 22:42, we find a parallel to Jesus' prayer in Mark 14:35, where he also prays that God's will be done rather than his own.
Matthew 26:39 gives a parallel account to Mark 14:35, where Jesus prays in Gethsemane and submits to God's will.
